label: Klila
note: Dried, unlike soft chhurpi or ayib; the closest relative is hard chhurpi

about.text: A very hard, dried cheese of eastern Algeria (and Morocco) made by heating lben until it curdles, draining the curd and drying it in the sun to under 10 % water.

links.name: Leksir & Chemmam 2015, Livestock Research for Rural Development 27(5)

how.label: heat, drain, sun-dry
how.text: Klila is made like soft buttermilk cheese, but the curd is cut and left in the sun until it is almost dry, so it keeps for months and was food for nomads and travellers. A separate account heats the whey of a curd at 50–60 °C for 30 min with no starter.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: Lben, the soured, churned milk, is moderately heated until it curdles.
In the sun to very hard pieces; exact temperatures and times are not reported.

facts.v: No coliforms, faecal streptococci, Salmonella or staphylococci found; total mesophiles about 10³ cfu/g
